summary: Aroostook County, ME: 1917-1920 tower history; sources disagree on whether it stands. The register point is on private land east of Masardis.

facts.design: 26-foot wood tower in the 1920 inventory; a 48-foot steel tower was partly erected in 1917
facts.status_note: The Forest Lookouts history lists the tower as removed, undated. The FFLA list shows a Squa-Pan tower standing at a different point with its cab gone. The register says it is not known whether Squa Pan still stands.

access.note: The register says the site is on private property.

events.note: 48-foot steel tower partly erected, completion planned for 1918
26-foot tower completed, per the 1918 Forest Commissioner's report as quoted by the Forest Lookouts history; type not stated

corrections.why: The register point says it is not known whether the tower still stands. The 'Removed' note in the Forest Lookouts history is undated and sits beside a 1920 inventory entry, so 'gone' is not confirmed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Unresolved: the register says unknown; the Forest Lookouts history says removed, undated; the FFA list shows a Squa-Pan point about 10 km north-west of the register point as standing with its cab gone. The story reports all three.
The register point (46.47929, -68.16667) and the FFA point (46.57080, -68.19996) differ; they are kept separate because it is not confirmed that they are the same tower.
Unresolved: a 48-foot steel tower was planned in 1917, and a 26-foot tower was completed in 1918 and listed as wood in 1920. The sources do not say whether these are the same tower.

notes_for_editor: Possibly the same tower as us-me-squa-pan-mountain (FFA point 46.57080, -68.19996, same Forest Lookouts history). The two records split the register point from the FFA point; editor should decide whether to merge. The register spells the town 'Marsardis'; the story uses Masardis. No staffing, fire or access-permission evidence found. Two searches turned up no further Squa Pan history.
